About a month ago I decided to play through Skyrim one more time with every mod that looked worthwhile. I spent a few days going through the nexus and watching youtube mod series while taking notes, and I thought I might save someone else like me the trouble:

First, I recommend Skyrim Mod Organizer over the Nexus Mod Manager, because SMO allows you to enable and disable mods without it actually copying any files around. This lets you have multiple mod profiles, and more importantly, it means at no point do actual files get overwritten, so it's easier to tweak things until they work if you've got problems. You do pay a small price in having to do a bit of extra work to get FNIS, ASIS or skyproc working because of that, but there are instructions available for that. Both tools come with nexus integration. Use NMO if you want, but you'd be insane to not use either.

First, a few crucial ones:

Unofficial Skyrim Legendary Edition Patch- modders these days pretty much assume you're using all the officially released mods for skyrim. If you're not, you'll have to get the most recent unofficial patch for whatever you've got.

SkyUI - don't play in PC without it, it also enables the mod configuration menu, so use it even if you don't like it

SKSE - prerequisite for all the more interesting mods

Crash fixes - it actually does fix some crashes. Read the nexus page, there are settings to set.

Also, you can optionally download TES5edit and clean the official mods, but I don't know if that actually gets you anything. This covers everything you might want to do on your virgin skyrim installation to prepare it for what's to come.

Now the rest in more or less the order of how interesting/fundamental I think they are:

Perkus Maximus - there are a few core gameplay/perk tree overhauls available, including sperg, requiem, and SkyRe, but PerMa hits the best point for me in terms of not requiring me to do tons of work to get other things to work with it and steering the game in a direction I like. PerMa has a compatability patch for making it work with other mods which is impressively thorough. In terms of what it does, the answer is "a lot", but what I like about it is that it makes most of the individual perks have a real gameplay impact rather than an incremental number increase. Some of them get pretty creative. Installation of this mod requires running an extra thing once all your other mods are in place to merge all the items they may have added into the perma system.

CBBE + Bodyslide- some of the more impressive custom armors require one of the custom bodies, this one seems the most compatible and popular, and with bodyslide you can customize your body as well as you could your face in vanilla. Bodyslide must be launched through the mod manager to actually do the customizing and set up whatever custom armors you've got. I also got vanilla outfits bodyslided, 2x clothing remix, and OCR clothing replacer to go with this, so the default armors would work appropriately and have higher resolution textures. Some of the fancier mods will expect/benefit from having HDT physics enabled, which is it's own whole set of things with instructions to follow. There are also animation replacers for just about any character animation in the game if you've gotten this deep into body replacement and have FNIS installed and working for the above stuff.

ApachiiSkyHair - the default hairs are just not great. These have a tendency to get a little on the korean MMO side of style choices, and some of them are doomed to armor clipping issues, but the default hair has just got to go and this is the best way to do it.

Weather system + ENB - Which one you pick is a matter of taste, I was a fan of Tetrachromatic ENB and NLVA, which is a modified form of Vivid Weather. Tetrachromatic favors a lot of color saturation, which I like in this context. It's made to work with NLVA, which adds a bunch of weather systems. A good ENB is the #1 most important thing for making skyrim look like it came out yesterday instead of several years ago, and also the #1 thing that will push your graphics card hard if you let it, so pick one that looks good to your taste but still fits your hardware. Note that the underlying tool for ENBs has been improved a lot over the years, so some of the most popular ones (and therefore oldest) ones on the nexus aren't actually as nice as some of the newer ones which take advantage of the newer features.

As a seperate note, I'll add that caution should be advised around the "realistic lighting" mods, some of which are ENBs. Some of them involve adding lights to practically every dungeon in the game which has obvious compatibility issues, and most/all of them basically make you blind in anything other than perfect daylight or rooms with approximately ten candles per square foot unless you crank your monitor brightness. I guess you're supposed to use a torch or magelight, but then everything's either too bright or pitch black with very little in between due to the way cast lighting drops off to zero beyond a short distance, thereby making the lighting even less "realistic" than default. Also it makes playing a vampire who is weak to daylight impossible without using vision modes constantly to see at night, at which point you might as well just not bother with all those mods that make the game actually look good, because you won't be seeing any of it.

Realistic Water Two - there are a few water mods to choose from, this is the one I liked. Makes the water flow slightly more realistically, and look a lot better.

If you're ambitious, get a the LOD patch. It's got a very exact installation procedure, but it definitely does improve how things look at a distance.

ASIS - adds nothing by itself, instead it crawls through all the stuff you've added for yourself through mods, like perks and spells, and lets NPCs use them. Must be activated through the mod manger.

Deadly Dragons - Adds a lot more dragon variety, and "assault events", where multiple dragons attack you at once. Definitely add this if you find normal dragons boring. Don't enable the deadly dragon armory, it's a good idea but it's not very well put together. I also added Elemental Dragons and used Mercy is for the Weak to patch them together.

Weapon + Armor Fixes Remade, Complete Crafting Overhaul Remade, Clothing and Clutter Fixes - these mods all kind of go together, they all exist to make the vanilla systems more consistent rather than totally redesign them, and they work alright with PerMa.

Royal Vampire Bloodlines + Better Vampires- these two mods can be compatible with each other, and they make being a vampire much more interesting and a lot more customizable. There are probably similar things available for werewolves.

Forgotten Magic Redone - there are several magic mods, but this one forgoes adding 100+ spells (which are frankly too many to manage in a realtime game anyway) for a small number of spells that had a lot more attention paid to them. The spells level up with use, and give you points which you can use to activate various modifiers.

Interesting NPCs - This mod is very large, and adds a lot of voiced NPCs with various things to say around the world, and a few quests attached to them. If you've already met everyone in skyrim, this will make meeting people new again.

Frostfall - Adds a cold survival element to the game. I understand this is a little script intensive, and maybe the gameplay it adds isn't for everyone, but it's worth trying.

A Quality World Map With Roads - there are a lot of map mods, some of them look like canvas, some of them look like a high-res satellite image, some have roads, some don't. Pick one of them.

Bound Armory - Custom smithed and enchanted weapons leave summoned weapons in the dust, this mod helps change that.

Skyrim Flora Overhaul, Unbelievable Grass Two - these two mods improve the plants and grass. There are other options for both, but getting something for more/better grass definitely improves the look of the game.

OBIS - adds a lot of new bandit types, themed into various "gangs". Makes meeting bandits less predictable.

Bijin wives/NPCs/warmaidens - These mods all update a handful of the more notable women in skyrim with ridiculously lifelike versions. I would be amazed if the guy who made these isn't in the industry already and doing this sort of thing for a living.

Inigo, Sofia - there are a lot of companion mods, some of them the work of very talented modelers/texture people, but these two have voice acting, so that sets them apart from most.

Immersive Amazing Follower Tweaks - there are several follower mods that improve how you can interact with followers, this is the one that's still updated and seems least likely to cause problems while still extending your options with followers.

Mysticism - The Lost Art - this mod adds a lot of stuff, but the only part of it I care about/use is that it makes it so you always put souls in gems of the right size, or else it cancels the soul capture. No more accidentally putting petty souls in grand soul gems. This should have been in the default game.

Legacy of the Dragonborn - adds a huge museum, with a spot to store every unique item in skyrim. Puts those dinky little display cases you might get in the fancier homes to shame. Worth it for the ability to put down those 20 pound elder scrolls alone.

I guess that's the character limit, more below.
In honor of a "new" version of Skyrim coming out, ~100 mods to make the original version interesting again

Warzones - adds big fights to some places in Skyrim. Makes it seem like sometimes stuff does actually happen without you doing it.

Achieve That - adds achievements to the game. Lots of them. Kind of a throwaway mod, but it can be fun to check all the stuff you've done. Also adds a kind of stat improvement system based on achievement points I recommend leaving alone for balance reasons.

World's Dawn - adds a whole new stat system on top of the existing one, some randomly generated enchanted gear on enemies at random, and the ability to augment your gear. Makes it slightly more worthwhile to check bodies after the early game, particularly with PerMa toning down blacksmithing and enchanting.

KenMOD Lockpick Pro Cheat - I have picked most of the locks in Oblivion more than once. And in Skyrim. And in Fallout 4. And in Fallout New Vegas. And in Fallout 3. And in Dying Light. I am fucking done with that style of lockpicking minigame. I can do it, I have shown I can do it, and I am not interested in doing it even one more time. So this adds a bar that just tells you where to put the pick. The way it does it is entirely transparent to any other mods you might have, so it's more compatible than any cheats that might try to just automatically open locks for you.

Wearable Lantern - adds a bit more light without taking up one of your hands.

Static Mesh Improvement Mod - Some corners were cut for performance reasons when it comes to some of the static meshes in Skyrim, this un-cuts those corners.

Spellcrafting for Skyrim - Adds a somewhat wonky but workable system for crafting your own spells at the college.

Immersive Idiots - Roderick Redbeard - I think Skyrim could use more bastards, this seems to be one. An unusual companion.

Winstad Mine - Instead of finding a mine you want and waiting outside of it for the ore to repopulate, just get this and have people mine it for you. It's not perfectly made, but it's functional and it gets you the ore you need in a less tedious way.

Quick loot - Fallout 4 style looting of containers without having to open them. Not entirely bug-free, but it works most of the time.

In terms of new armor or weapons, anything by DeserterX or Favored Soul, though you do have to jump through some minor hoops to actually get it in game with stats that let you use them.

And now some mods that add actual new content- I recommend turning these on as necessary, since there is a limit to how many huge mods you can stick on Skyrim at once before it becomes unstable. If things get unstable, turn some of them back off.

Heimfeigr, Falskaar, Spectraverse, Tel Nalta II, Dwemertech, Wheels of lull, Wyrmstooth, Summerset Isle, Pirates of Skyrim, anything this guy has made a typo patch for. I haven't yet gotten to any of these in my playthrough with all the above mods on, so I can't comment on these yet myself.
Just a quick note, but soon NMM will have most if not all of the features of Mod Organizer because they hired the guy who wrote Mod Organizer to work on NMM. No official release date yet though.
